- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp drop, model tends to underestimate future price — correct by adding 1–2% to forecasted lows.
- After a price spike (forecast > 65), model often overcorrects downward — adjust by +1–3% to prevent premature reversal.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.3) and forecast is rising, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with bearish sentiment.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — apply +0.5–1.5% bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.25), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- If forecasted price is below 60 and sentiment is positive, model is too pessimistic — increase by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model often misses mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >65 and true price drops below 62, adjust downward by 2–4% to reflect momentum correction.
